## Purpose

Lift a parent episode's human `hold` when its operator is ready to resume.
Engine rollback preserves human gates, so this explicit release also recovers
a held parent that has been transferred back to legacy integration.

## When a playbook uses it

Playbooks cannot invoke this human control. Only the local human operator may
preview or apply a release; supervisors, workers and daemon services are refused.

## How it works internally

The handler in `src/commands/integration_commands.py` validates the request and
local principal. `GatePrimitives.release_hold` in `src/integration/gates.py`
takes the exclusive parent engine lock, then locks and rechecks the live subject,
its version, current gate and journal identity. Apply requires the previewed
version and a nonblank reason. Only an immutable `hold` answer is releasable.

## Side effects and persistence

The transaction appends `gate-release:<gate_id>` to the subject journal with the
operator, reason, original answer and exact head/generation/policy. It clears
`integration_subjects.gate_id`, increments the subject version and schedules a
fresh visit. The engine, original gate definition, answer, dashboard projection,
receipts and product pauses remain intact. If the underlying failure persists,
the reconciler asks a new gate rather than reusing the released answer.

## Failure modes and diagnostics

`refused` includes missing reason/version, stale subject, a gate that is no
longer current, unanswered or non-hold gates, terminal/non-parent subjects and
changed head/generation/policy. A stale apply requires a fresh preview.
`unauthorized` requires a local human operator. Generic gate resolution and
projection expiry cannot release this hold.

## Example step

This command is operator-only. Preview, then apply with the returned version:

```sh
aq integration release-held-gate SUBJECT_ID GATE_ID
aq integration release-held-gate SUBJECT_ID GATE_ID \
  --expected-version VERSION --reason "ready to resume collection" --apply
```
